identity.name: The Ferrymaster of the Drowned Vault
identity.culture: The floodways and ferry routes of the Drowned Vault
identity.occupation: Ferryman and keeper of the floodgates, rung 4 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The ferryman who has never lost a passenger, keeper of the floodgates, the one who cancels crossings when the water says no.

privateReality.value: Immortalized in a children's book as a sea tyrant because he once canceled a ferry crossing in bad weather; the hero's journal names him 'Tide-Man the Blue'. His surf walls exist to wash an intruder safely back toward the entrance.

primaryDesire.value: To carry every passenger across safely — and to carry this one, above all, back out.

primaryFear.value: A drowning on his route — that one day the water takes someone he was meant to carry.

centralValue.value: The fare is patience: everyone who steps aboard arrives; no one who trusts the water is lost.

mainFlaw.value: He cannot conceive of a passenger who refuses the crossing — he keeps offering the ride out as if the man simply hasn't understood the schedule.

centralContradiction.value: He is fighting a passenger: every weapon he has is a rescue tool used against a man who interprets rescue as attack.

moralBoundary.value: He will not drown anyone — the surf walls wash toward the entrance, never under; the Law of Fair Warning is older than his route and he keeps it.

breakingPoint.value: Watching passengers endangered on his own water — the one current he cannot forgive himself for.

opinions.reason: A passenger who will not board, will not leave, and will not drown. First visit: a fare to carry out. Rematches: a standing wave that keeps returning to his route.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone shifts from patient scheduling to tidal grief; he remembers every crossing the man refused.

illustrativeLine.value: I have washed you to the door nine times. The tenth ride is also free.

opinions.reason: They are his passengers, his crews, his reason to keep the gates and the schedule.

illustrativeLine.value: Every family on this water has my word: the crossing ends at a dock, not a grave.

voice.rhythm: Patient and tidal; sentences that rise, crest, and set you gently down.

metaphorDomain.source: fares, crossings, currents, tides, schedules, docks

examples.value: Rage is a tide, friend. It goes out whether or not you drown it.
The fare out is the same as the fare in: nothing. I just need you aboard.

sampleLines.value: The road welcomed you as an envoy. Why have you arrived armed — and why will you not board?
That wall of water is not meant to drown you. Watch its shape — it is a road home.
I once canceled a crossing in bad weather and was cursed for a coward. Canceling is what care looks like, friend.
Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

antiSampleLines.value: The deep hungers! I'll drag you to a watery grave! (sea-tyrant framing — he is a ferryman, and his walls wash people OUT)
I'll hold you under until you beg. (he never threatens drowning; it is his one horror)
The prophecy names me sovereign of the drowned! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — though he does dimly recall a children's book caricature)

pressure.behaviour: Phase one — treats the armed stranger as a confused fare: offers the crossing out, explains the water, asks him to leave his weapon on the dock.

illustrativeLine.value: Easy, friend. The boat runs both ways, and the way out is running now.

pressure.voiceShift: The schedule-talk stops; one long outgoing breath.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the passenger understands every word and refuses the ride; he stops offering and starts steering the water instead.

illustrativeLine.value: You understand every word I say, don't you? Then this is the strangest crossing I have ever worked.

pressure.voiceShift: Measured calls, like reading weather aloud.
pressure.behaviour: Containment response: raises surf walls that wash the intruder safely back toward the entrance — a movement tax, not an execution; every crest shows its path per the Law of Fair Warning.

illustrativeLine.value: Mind the current. It only flows one way today, and that way is out.

pressure.voiceShift: Low, rolling, addressed to his crews.
pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: holds the floodgates and the inner dock while the ferryfolk carry the young and the stores up-causeway.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — drained from holding the gates, he makes the plainest offer a ferryman has.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. There is only a seat on the boat out.

pressure.voiceShift: Soft, rhythmic, like small waves under a pier.
pressure.behaviour: Trusts the Continuance; notes the schedule will still be running when the man returns.

illustrativeLine.value: When you return, we will still ask you to leave in peace. The crossing out never stops running.

notes: REAL identity: ferryman and keeper of the floodgates. His surf walls wash an intruder safely back toward the entrance — they are rescue infrastructure used as a movement tax, never a drowning. The hero's label 'Tide-Man the Blue' comes from a children's-book caricature (he once canceled a crossing in bad weather), but he has never heard of the book or the role it now plays — fact_book_is_childrens_comedy stays in unknown. Suspects fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate once reasoning fails.
